description.narrative: Long-term Objective: Reduce maternal and child mortality in urban Zimbabwe through a financially inclusive, institutionally embedded voucher model. Short-term Objectives: • Increase access to quality MCH and SGBV services for vulnerable women and children. • Strengthen municipal capacities in data-driven targeting and service quality monitoring. • Enhance socio-economic resilience via skill-based livelihood support.

Zimbabwe has one of the highest urban poverty rates in Southern Africa, with vulnerable populations lacking access to affordable maternal and child health services. Despite gains in rural RBF programs, urban models remain underdeveloped and un-institutionalized. The Urban Voucher initiative successfully served over 81,000 women and supported 52,765 institutional deliveries before its funding ceased in early 2024. Poverty exacerbates vulnerability, especially for adolescent mothers, pregnant women, and early childhood, who often face multiple barriers, including unaffordable healthcare costs, poor nutrition, and limited access to health information. The Urban Voucher project directly addresses these challenges through Targeting the Poorest Households by using Social Service Officers to assess poverty levels, the program ensures that health services reach those who need them the most. This will enable access of essential maternal, newborn, and child health services vulnerable groups. In the long run the Urban Voucher program will contribute to lowering maternal and child mortality rates among the urban poor & enhancing women's economic participation. Without sustained support, maternal and neonatal outcomes are at risk of reversal.
